answer: Surge-priced admission: the cost of joining, measured in graded original work before a seat can earn, rises automatically whenever new sign-ups spike above the network's normal pulse. A few honest newcomers pay a small entry fee in effort. A sybil wave of thousands drives the price up for every seat it adds, so each fake costs more than the last. The work done is kept in a public vault and checked for overlap, so cheap rewrites don't count, and a mass-joining attacker faces a long, costly voyage.
